## Simplified explanation

body:
Which statements are true about a parallelogram?

I. Pairs of opposite sides are parallel.
II. Adjacent sides are perpendicular.
III. Pairs of adjacent sides are transversals to pairs of opposite sides.
hint: Work it out step by step.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Opposite sides are parallel, so each side cuts across (is a transversal to) the pair of sides it meets. Adjacent sides are perpendicular only in rectangles/squares.

## Simplified explanation

Not all parallelograms have right angles.

body: Find the area of a square plot of land whose diagonal is 16 m.
hint: Work it out step by step.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Area $= \tfrac12 d^2 = \tfrac12(256) = 128$ m² (side $= 16/\sqrt2$).

## Simplified explanation

Area of a square = half the diagonal squared.

body: Which relationship holds between the circumference $C$ and area $A$ of a circle of radius $r$?
hint: Work it out step by step.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

$r = \dfrac{C}{2\pi}$, so $A = \pi r^2 = \pi\dfrac{C^2}{4\pi^2} = \dfrac{C^2}{4\pi}$.

## Simplified explanation

Eliminate $r$.

body: What is the size of an interior angle (to 1 d.p.) of a regular heptagon?
hint: Work it out step by step.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

$\dfrac{(7-2)180°}{7} = \dfrac{900°}{7} = 128.6°$.

## Simplified explanation

$(n-2)180°/n$.

body: Given triangle $ABC$ with $A(-2, 2)$, $B(1, 4)$ and $C(2, 1)$: (a) calculate $|AB|$, $|BC|$, $|AC|$; (b) what type of triangle is $ABC$? (c) Determine the equation of $\overline{AC}$.
answer:
**(a)** $|AB| = \sqrt{3^2 + 2^2} = \sqrt{13} \approx 3.61$; $|BC| = \sqrt{1^2 + (-3)^2} = \sqrt{10} \approx 3.16$; $|AC| = \sqrt{4^2 + (-1)^2} = \sqrt{17} \approx 4.12$.

**(b)** All sides differ → **scalene**. ($13 + 10 = 23 \ne 17$, so not right-angled; in fact all angles are acute since $13 + 10 > 17$.)

**(c)** $m_{AC} = \dfrac{1 - 2}{2 + 2} = -\tfrac14$; $y - 2 = -\tfrac14(x + 2) \Rightarrow x + 4y - 6 = 0$.

> [!answer]
> $\sqrt{13}, \sqrt{10}, \sqrt{17}$; scalene (acute); $x + 4y - 6 = 0$.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Distance formula, then point–slope form.

## Simplified explanation

Use $\sqrt{(x_2-x_1)^2 + (y_2-y_1)^2}$.
hint: Show every step.

body: Construct triangle $PQR$ with $|PQ| = 12.5$ cm, $|PR| = 9.5$ cm and $\angle QPR = 60°$. Measure $\angle QRP$ and $\angle PQR$, construct the circumcircle and state its radius.
answer:
**Construction:** draw $PQ = 12.5$ cm; construct $60°$ at $P$ (equilateral-arc method); mark $R$ on the arm with $PR = 9.5$ cm; join $QR$. Bisect any two sides perpendicularly; their intersection $O$ is the circumcentre; draw the circle with radius $OP$.

**Expected measurements** (by the cosine/sine rules, for checking): $QR^2 = 12.5^2 + 9.5^2 - 2(12.5)(9.5)\cos60° = 127.75 \Rightarrow QR \approx 11.3$ cm; $\angle QRP \approx 73.4°$, $\angle PQR \approx 46.6°$; radius $R = \dfrac{QR}{2\sin60°} \approx 6.5$ cm.

> [!answer]
> ∠QRP ≈ 73°, ∠PQR ≈ 47°, circumradius ≈ 6.5 cm (accept small drawing tolerances).
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

The circumcentre is where perpendicular bisectors of the sides meet.

## Simplified explanation

Bisect two sides; where they cross is the centre.
hint: Show every step.

body: A circle circumscribes a square plot EFGH of side 2.8 m. Calculate the area of one segment (between a side of the square and the circle). Take $\pi = 3.142$.
answer:
Diagonal $= 2.8\sqrt2$, so $r = 1.4\sqrt2$ and $r^2 = 3.92$ m².

Circle area $= 3.142 \times 3.92 = 12.317$ m²; square area $= 2.8^2 = 7.84$ m².

Four equal segments: $12.317 - 7.84 = 4.477$; one segment $= 4.477 \div 4 \approx 1.12$ m².

> [!answer]
> ≈ 1.12 m²
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Each segment is a quarter of (circle − square); equivalently sector (90°) − triangle.

## Simplified explanation

Circle minus square, divided by 4.
hint: Show every step.

body: The vertices of triangle $ABC$ are $A(0, 2)$, $B(1, 5)$, $C(-1, 4)$. (i) Find $|AB|$, $|AC|$, $|BC|$ and the type of triangle. (ii) Find its perimeter.
answer:
$|AB| = \sqrt{1 + 9} = \sqrt{10}$; $|AC| = \sqrt{1 + 4} = \sqrt5$; $|BC| = \sqrt{4 + 1} = \sqrt5$.

$|AC| = |BC|$ → **isosceles**; also $AC^2 + BC^2 = 10 = AB^2$, so it is a **right-angled isosceles** triangle (right angle at $C$).

Perimeter $= \sqrt{10} + 2\sqrt5 \approx 3.162 + 4.472 = 7.63$ units.

> [!answer]
> Right-angled isosceles triangle; perimeter ≈ 7.63 units.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Check both equal sides and Pythagoras.

## Simplified explanation

Compare squared lengths.
hint: Show every step.

body: A hexagon has $x°$ as the value of three of its interior angles. Two of the remaining angles are each double the size of the three equal angles, and the sixth angle is $160°$. (i) Find $x$. (ii) Find the exterior angle corresponding to the largest interior angle.
answer:
Hexagon angle sum $= (6-2)180° = 720°$: $3x + 2(2x) + 160 = 720 \Rightarrow 7x = 560 \Rightarrow x = 80$.

Angles: $80°, 80°, 80°, 160°, 160°, 160°$. Largest $= 160°$; exterior $= 180° - 160° = 20°$.

> [!answer]
> $x = 80$; exterior angle $= 20°$.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Sum of interior angles = $(n-2)180°$.

## Simplified explanation

Set up an equation for the angle sum.
hint: Show every step.

body: $P(-2, 3)$, $Q(0, -3)$ and $R(-1, -1)$ are the vertices of triangle $PQR$. (a) Find $|PQ|$, $|PR|$, $|RQ|$ and the type of triangle. (b) Find the equation of the line through $P$ perpendicular to $\overline{PQ}$.
answer:
**(a)** $|PQ| = \sqrt{4 + 36} = \sqrt{40} = 2\sqrt{10} \approx 6.32$; $|PR| = \sqrt{1 + 16} = \sqrt{17} \approx 4.12$; $|RQ| = \sqrt{1 + 4} = \sqrt5 \approx 2.24$. All different → **scalene** (and $17 + 5 < 40$, so obtuse-angled at $R$).

**(b)** $m_{PQ} = \dfrac{-3 - 3}{0 + 2} = -3$, so the perpendicular gradient is $\tfrac13$: $y - 3 = \tfrac13(x + 2) \Rightarrow x - 3y + 11 = 0$.

> [!answer]
> Scalene (obtuse) triangle; $x - 3y + 11 = 0$.
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Perpendicular gradients multiply to −1.

## Simplified explanation

Negative reciprocal of $m_{PQ}$.
hint: Show every step.

body: Construct parallelogram $CDEF$ with $|CD| = 9$ cm, $\angle FCD = 105°$ and diagonal $|DF| = 12$ cm. Measure $\angle ECD$; construct the perpendicular from $E$ to $CD$ meeting it at $M$; measure $|EM|$ and find the area of $CDEF$.
answer:
**Construction:** draw $CD = 9$ cm; construct $105°$ at $C$ ($90° + 15°$); with centre $D$ and radius 12 cm cut the arm at $F$; complete the parallelogram ($DE \parallel CF$, $FE \parallel CD$). Drop the perpendicular from $E$ to $CD$ produced.

**Expected values** (by sine rule in $\triangle CDF$): $|CF| \approx 5.9$ cm, $\angle ECD \approx 37.6°$, $|EM| \approx 5.7$ cm; area $= |CD| \times |EM| \approx 9 \times 5.74 \approx 51.7$ cm².

> [!answer]
> ∠ECD ≈ 38°, EM ≈ 5.7 cm, area ≈ 51.7 cm² (allow drawing tolerance).
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Area of a parallelogram = base × perpendicular height.

## Simplified explanation

105° = 90° + 15° (bisect 30°).
hint: Show every step.

body: (a) Show that the volume $V$, curved surface area $S$, height $H$ and slant height $L$ of a cone satisfy $V = \dfrac{S^2 H}{3\pi L^2}$. (b) A cylindrical metal bowl of radius 2.1 m and height 5.0 m is melted and recast into a cuboid of cross-sectional area 9.0 m². Using $\pi = \tfrac{22}{7}$, find (i) the height of the cuboid; (ii) its total surface area if its width is 1.2 m.
answer:
**(a)** $S = \pi r L \Rightarrow r = \dfrac{S}{\pi L}$. Then $V = \tfrac13\pi r^2 H = \tfrac13\pi\dfrac{S^2}{\pi^2 L^2}H = \dfrac{S^2 H}{3\pi L^2}$.

**(b)(i)** $V = \tfrac{22}{7}(2.1)^2(5) = 69.3$ m³; height $= 69.3 \div 9 = 7.7$ m.

**(ii)** Cross-section $l \times w = 9 \Rightarrow l = 9 \div 1.2 = 7.5$ m. TSA $= 2(lw + lh + wh) = 2(9 + 57.75 + 9.24) = 151.98$ m².

> [!answer]
> Height 7.7 m; total surface area ≈ 152.0 m².
explanation:
## Advanced explanation

Volume is conserved when recasting.

## Simplified explanation

Eliminate $r$ using $S = \pi r L$.
hint: Show every step.
